newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen up $0.50-$1 - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen up $0.50-$1 - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Friday were expected up $0.50 to $1.00 per cwt amid continued strong packer demand and light marketings, according to livestock dealers.
Top prices in Iowa and southern Minnesota for hogs delivered at the plant could range from $57.50 to $58.50.
Illinois top hog prices at the plant were seen up $0.50 at $58.50 and Indiana/Ohio top prices at the plant were expected at $57.00, the dealers said.
Strong pork demand was fueling the interest for hogs, led by gains in fresh hams and pork bellies, market sources said.
Strength also was tied to reduced marketings, some of which was attributed to producers holding animals back in anticipation of higher prices following Friday's USDA quarterly hog inventory report.
The report is expected to show hog supplies three to four percent below year ago levels, according to trade estimates.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota hog receipts Wednesday totaled 104,000 head, below that day's estimate of 110,000. Thursday's estimate was 105,000 head, USDA said.
